target_customer: Medical device and medtech companies and their field sales representatives
problem: Medtech field reps lose time logging visits and follow-ups in CRM systems. Obento offers a mobile, voice-driven CRM co-pilot that automates documentation and follow-ups.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to medtech sales organizations, pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: Mobile CRM co-pilot for medtech sales

founders.name: Naxin Wang
founders.background_notes: YC page says trained as an analyst and built products at Verily for biopharma and medtech customers; a search listing says product manager and analytics manager roles at Verily.

technical_complexity.rationale: A voice-to-CRM mobile assistant on top of language models and existing CRM integrations is mostly application engineering.

defensibility.rationale: CRM integrations and workflow data could create some stickiness, but large CRM vendors and other startups can build similar assistants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows incumbents copying or buying Obento.

market_need_then: Medtech field sales reps carry heavy documentation work, which is the pain the company cites; no independent demand data was opened.

branding.domain_note: Company contact on the YC page uses obentohealth.com; getobento.com is the listed website and gobento.com belongs to an unrelated service.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material found, and the name is confusable with an unrelated Bento service.

outcome_analysis: Obento Health is listed Active with a team of two per the YC page and has no found coverage of funding, exit or shutdown. The idea targets a clear workflow pain for medtech reps and the founder has Verily medtech and biopharma product experience, but incumbents like Salesforce and Veeva sell medtech CRMs. Too little public information exists to explain the outcome.
notes: Company website getobento.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch, so it was not read; the site may be down. Aggregators (CB Insights, PitchBook, StartupIntros) show about $500K from Y Combinator in August or September 2023, with conflicting labels; treated as YC standard deal and unverified, so no round recorded. Rodrigo Gutierrez, former Strava product engineering lead per the launch post, is described as an early employee and is not listed as co-founder. Some aggregators describe the company as digital storefronts for health products, which conflicts with YC and is treated as unreliable. No dated competitor source found, so the list is empty.
